findings_to_judge.finding: Waterdrop's Q1 2026 net profit FELL 8.9% year over year to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m, and operating profit rose only 5.4% (RMB80.0m vs RMB75.9m) on revenue up 64.8%, because sales and marketing expense tripled — up 213.8% to RMB541.1m from RMB172.4m, or 43.6% of revenue — so the entire 'AI-driven growth' story is currently producing no incremental profit, and the Q2 2026 comparative is Q2 2025's RMB140.2m, 42% above the Q1 2026 run-rate.

Waterdrop's current US$50m share repurchase authorisation runs 'during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026' — expiring the day AFTER this 2026-09-08 print — and it has been almost unused: cumulative repurchases went from approximately US$109.0m (55.7m ADSs) at 2025-08-31 to approximately US$120.1m (61.8m ADSs) at 2026-05-31, so roughly US$11m of the US$50m was spent in nine months; the company has launched a new programme every September for five straight years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and announced the 2025 one inside the Q2 earnings release itself, and its semi-annual dividend's second-half tranche has likewise been declared with the September release (ex-dates 2024-10-11 and 2025-10-10), where US$0.03 per ADS is now 2.86% of a US$1.0495 spot versus roughly 1.5% a year ago.

China's eight financial and internet regulators jointly issued the Administrative Measures for Online Marketing of Financial Products on 2026-04-24, effective 2026-09-30 — 22 days after this print — whose Article 20 bars third-party internet platforms (defined as sites and apps 'not self-operated by a financial institution') from intervening or covertly intervening in sales-contract signing, fund transfer or suitability assessment, and from conducting interactive consultation with consumers about financial products, which puts a hard compliance date on the traffic architecture behind Waterdrop's insurance marketplace and its non-licensed Waterdrop Medical Crowdfunding funnel.

Waterdrop turned over both of its finance-oversight seats in the five weeks immediately before this print: independent director Heping Feng left the board effective 2026-07-01 and was replaced by Qianfei Chang as independent director and audit committee chair (6-K, 2026-06-23), and then the vice president of finance and head of finance, Xiaoying Xu, resigned effective 2026-07-31 (6-K, 2026-07-24).
